rows.name: provenance as declared
rows.saw: exit 0; node table True, chain True, fixtures True

rows.name: BREAK: a node renamed in the workflow
rows.ran: rename 'Sim 1' in a copy of the workflow, run verify-provenance

rows.name: BREAK: Sim 3 skipped in the connections
rows.ran: rewire Sim 2 straight to Aggregate in a copy, run verify-provenance

rows.name: BREAK: a fixture changed after it was frozen
rows.ran: change one digit in c01, run verify-provenance

rows.name: BREAK: the validator on the changed fixture
every catalogued defect rejected, for its own reason
rows.saw: exit 1; 10/10 rejected; wrong or missing reasons: none
rows.expected: exit 1 (by design); 10/10 rejected, each for its catalogued reason

rows.name: the contract has not drifted from the workflow's own rules
rows.ran: compare the validator's five messages with the errors.push() messages in the Parse & Validate Input node
rows.expected: the same five messages in the same order

rows.name: approved tools run on the clean set
rows.ran: run-approved-tools on the validated clean set
rows.saw: exit 0; 15 results, each with an aggregate and a prompt: True

rows.name: the clean set reaches every branch
rows.ran: read the results: matrix cells, risk appetites, horizons, final recommendations
rows.saw: 9/9 matrix cells; 3/3 risk appetites; 3/3 horizons; 5/5 final recommendations

rows.name: BREAK: the tools are handed rejected requests
BREAK: a clean file hand-edited to hold a rejected request
rows.ran: add one rejected entry to the clean validated.json, run-approved-tools

rows.name: parity with the original JavaScript
rows.ran: parity-check: original JS vs the port, 23 requests (15 clean, 8 object-shaped defective)
rows.saw: parity: 23/23 requests identical to the original JavaScript, 0 different

rows.name: BREAK: rounding with Python's round() (half goes to even)
rows.ran: parity-check on a copy of the port with that one change
rows.saw: parity: 22/23 requests identical to the original JavaScript, 1 different
rows.expected: exit 1; the parity check must catch it

rows.name: BREAK: toFixed with Python's format (ties go to even)
rows.ran: parity-check on a copy of the port with that one change
rows.saw: parity: 19/23 requests identical to the original JavaScript, 4 different
rows.expected: exit 1; the parity check must catch it

rows.name: BREAK: Math.min/Math.max replaced by Python's min/max (NaN is not contagious)
rows.ran: parity-check on a copy of the port with that one change
rows.saw: parity: 21/23 requests identical to the original JavaScript, 2 different
rows.expected: exit 1; the parity check must catch it

rows.name: BREAK: numbers printed the Python way (100.0 for 100)
rows.ran: parity-check on a copy of the port with that one change
rows.saw: parity: 6/23 requests identical to the original JavaScript, 17 different
rows.expected: exit 1; the parity check must catch it
